payload.title: Glossary and do-not-translate list
payload.description:
As a publication editor, I want to decide how my terms are translated, so names and product words stay consistent and the translator is told only what it needs.

Design: section 2.4. Guideline kind `glossary`, publication then section scope. Entry: `{ source term, language, target term | doNotTranslate, note, caseSensitive, scope }`; people, organisations and products default to do-not-translate; an entry can give the approved local form and whether the original follows in brackets on first mention. Two uses: in the translator's prompt (only the entries whose source term occurs in the blocks) and in the check (the bilingual `parity` detector). Learning offers, never applies. Per Ryan 2026-11-13 the glossary and pack are where target-locale naming conventions live.

```gherkin
Feature: A publication decides how its terms are translated
  Scenario: The translator is told only the terms it will meet
    Given a glossary of forty entries
    And a block that contains two of the source terms
    When the block is translated
    Then the translator receives those two entries

  Scenario: A corrector's repeated fix is offered as an entry
    Given a corrector has changed "消融" to "abliteration" in two Stories
    When they save the second correction
    Then the console offers to add the term to the glossary
    And nothing is added until a person accepts

  Scenario: Names default to do-not-translate
    Given an organisation name with no glossary entry
    When a Story naming it is translated
    Then the name appears unchanged in the translation

  Scenario: A locale's approved form of a name is used
    Given the glossary gives an approved Chinese form of an organisation's name
    When a Story naming it is translated
    Then the approved form is used
    And the original follows in brackets on first mention if the entry says so
```
